subject.title: feat: sleep tool — pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` tool, and if so should it be a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted `agentTurn` with explicit sandbox policy?
rationale: The PR adds model-facing core scheduling behavior across gateway cron, session state, interruption, restart, and sandbox boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and security semantics.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require a revised implementation that targets the caller session, proves interrupt and restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

options.title: Keep existing cron/session guidance
options.body: Reject a new core tool for now and route delayed work through cron, process completion wakes, and `sessions_yield` where those surfaces already have ownership.

options.title: Narrow to an extension seam
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension point instead of bundling a default core tool if maintainers want optional scheduling behavior outside the default tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction but require a revised implementation that targets the caller session, proves interrupt and restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent runtime, cron, sandbox, live-probe, and docs history make this the strongest available routing owner for the product/API choice.
